extracted.intended_audience: inventors, patent practitioners, and legal professionals seeking practical guidance on drafting specifications and obtaining patents (England)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on what to include in a patent specification and the procedural steps to obtain letters patent under English practice (including enrolment, caveats, and territorial scope). Focuses on sufficiency of disclosure, novelty of combinations, and formal requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim only the invention
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing more than the invention must be claimed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Every old part which is essential and material in producing the intended effect will be considered as claimed if it be not designated as old. Do not claim more than what you actually invented; explicitly identify older elements to avoid implying they are claimed.

rubrics_metrics.name: New combination of known parts may be patentable
rubrics_metrics.description: A novel conformation (combination) of parts may constitute a new machine even though each part individually was known.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the new conformation of all those parts was of the inventor's invention, he may be entitled to a patent for the machine composed by that new conformation. But if another person had previously combined those parts up to a point and the inventor merely took up that combination and only added further combinations, the inventor cannot validly claim the whole as his invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not claim whole when only an improvement
rubrics_metrics.description: If the inventor has only invented an improvement of an old engine/manufacture, a specification claiming the whole will be bad.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the invention is merely an improvement of an existing device (e.g., Heathcote's engine), the specification must not claim the entire prior machine as the inventor's; improvements should be limited to the newly invented part or combination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe only the new combinations when adding to old manufactures
rubrics_metrics.description: If the invention consists of a new set of combinations added to a manufacture composed of combinations, the specification should describe only the new combinations and how they are to be added to the old ones.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not re-describe or attempt to appropriate the old combinations; explain how the new combinations integrate with the pre-existing manufacture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference to expired or purchased patents can suffice when combining their subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: If the combination consists of the subjects of several patents which have expired, or of some new ones that have been bought, a description of the method by which they were combined with a reference to the several specifications may be sufficient to sustain the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rather than re-specifying previously patented material, refer to the earlier specifications and focus disclosure on the novel manner of combination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method patents must be described as tangible means and be fully practicable
rubrics_metrics.description: A method merely as such cannot properly be the subject of a patent; where a patent is granted for a method it is in fact for the tangible means of carrying that method into practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The specification of a method must be as clear and evident as for a machine or manufacture: so accurate that no experiments are necessary to learn it and to put it in practice as beneficially as the patentee enjoys it. Governed by the same rules as machines and combinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chemical inventions must disclose substance and process
rubrics_metrics.description: When a chemical discovery is the foundation of the invention, the substance or thing produced (not merely the principle) ought to be described.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the ingredients, their proportions, the times of mixing, the best modes of making and using it, and the beneficial uses to which the substance can be applied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign inventions introduced into England must be fully and correctly explained
rubrics_metrics.description: A manufacture or machine first introduced into England, even if an improvement or a combination of native discoveries, must be fully and correctly explained in the specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The specification is regulated by the same laws and subject to the same critical examination as an English invention; describe every new part however minute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe every new part however minute
rubrics_metrics.description: Every part which is new, however minute, must be clearly described.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not omit tiny but novel elements; even small new features must be disclosed clearly to satisfy the public disclosure requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification of substances: state simplest elements and best modes
rubrics_metrics.description: In the specification of a substance, the simplest elements of which it can be formed, and the best modes of making and using it, must be accurately stated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide decomposition into elemental components and practical methods for production and use to enable the public to make and use the invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Machine descriptions: materials, proportions, modes, and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: In descriptions of machines there must with scrupulous fidelity be set forth the cheapest materials, the most exact proportions of the parts, the most expeditious and the best mode of conducting them, with the precise times of putting on, or taking off, any part of the machine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give practical construction and operational details (materials, dimensions/proportions, sequence/timing) so that the public can reproduce the invention and enjoy it as the patentee does.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep new combination or improvement distinct from the old manufacture
rubrics_metrics.description: An improvement or new combination must be kept distinctly apart from the old manufacture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly distinguish and identify the invented features vs prior manufacture so the scope of the claim and the disclosure are not conflated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public must be put in possession as ample and beneficial as patentee enjoys
rubrics_metrics.description: The public must be put in possession of the manufacture in a way as ample and beneficial as the patentee enjoys it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclosure must be sufficiently enabling that the public can practice the invention to the same beneficial degree as the patentee; the specification's purpose is public benefit as much as patentee protection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification formalities: inventor's hand and seal; drawings and references
rubrics_metrics.description: The specification must be under the hand and seal of the inventor and is sometimes accompanied with a design or drawing in the margin, to which references must be made from the body of the patent to render the whole intelligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure signature/acknowledgement formalities are met and include drawings with clear cross-references when needed for intelligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enrollment and timing requirements for the specification
rubrics_metrics.description: The specification must be enrolled within the time stated in the patent (formerly four months, now generally one month; extended to six months if inventor files affidavit intending patents for Scotland and Ireland). The specification must be acknowledged before a Master in Chancery and lodged in the Enrolment Office before the expiration of the time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely enrollment is mandatory; the given day is inclusive; Attorney General may enlarge the period before sealing; once the patent is sealed the date cannot be altered and legislative relief is required if time has expired. If defects occur, it is advisable in practice to conceal the invention and begin de novo with another petition to remedy defects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specifications are public and concealment is exceptional
rubrics_metrics.description: Specifications are kept open for inspection by the public and copies may be obtained; attempts to dispense with enrolment or conceal the specification have generally been unsuccessful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concealment of the specification is only permitted in very exceptional circumstances (e.g., special Act of Parliament); the enrolment exists for the benefit of the public to avoid wasting labour on already-patented inventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caveat practice: notice instrument and its effect
rubrics_metrics.description: A caveat is an instrument by which notice is requested to be given to the person who enters it whenever any application is made for a patent for a certain invention described in general terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One caveat is left at the chambers of the Attorney General and another at those of the Solicitor General; caveats must be annually renewed. If a similar patent is applied for, parties are summoned and separately examined; the caveat does not create any right but requests information and preference. Those opposing a patent need only show an interest. If a disappointed party believes he was injured after hearing, his remedy is by scire facias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Territorial extent and separate patents for Scotland/Ireland
rubrics_metrics.description: Privileges derived from a patent take effect only in England; if the Colonies are named they are included. To exercise exclusivity over the United Kingdom, separate patents must be taken out for Scotland and Ireland.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An Act of Parliament can preserve exclusive privilege in other places under the government's authority (e.g., West Indies). When applying for extended territorial coverage, state it in the petition and, for certain procedures (e.g., extending enrolment time), file necessary affidavits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition and affidavit procedural requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The first step is to present a petition to the King reciting that the petitioner is the true and first inventor of something likely to be of general benefit and praying for letters patent; an affidavit sworn before a Master in Chancery must accompany and support the allegations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The petition and affidavit are left at the Secretary of State's office; after a few days the petition is referred to the Attorney or Solicitor General for opinion, whose report typically recommends grant provided a particular description be enrolled within a given time — thus giving rise to the specification. Follow the prescribed forms and offices (see Appendix forms).

rubrics_metrics.name: Bill, warrant, and sealing process for the patent
rubrics_metrics.description: After the Attorney General's report a warrant is issued for a bill to prepare the grant for the royal signature; the bill (rough draft of the patent) is examined by law officers and passed through the Secretary of State, signet office, privy seal, and Lord Chancellor's patent office, where the patent is made out and sealed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The bill contains the allegations and the time for enrolment. Once a patent has passed the great seal its date cannot be altered. Follow the formal routings and have the specification prepared for enrolment in due time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acts of Parliament for special relief (e.g., prolonging term, assigning to many persons)
rubrics_metrics.description: Private Acts of Parliament can be obtained to prolong the term of a patent or to permit transfers/assignments beyond statutory limits, subject to statutory procedure (notice, petition, select committees, readings, and royal assent).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notices must be published (e.g., London Gazette, Edinburgh/Dublin papers when applicable), petitions must state dates and reasons (expense, capital required, improvements), witnesses examined by select committees, and the act often requires enrolment of an updated specification of the improved invention. Such acts do not validate patents beyond their lawful effect prior to the act.
